name: Minnis Bay Bar & Brasserie
summary: Shepherd Neame bar and big restaurant right on the Minnis Bay seafront, with a summer kiosk for ice cream and pizza.
description: The Minnis, as locals call it, is the main place to eat and drink on the front at Minnis Bay. It belongs to the Faversham brewer Shepherd Neame, which refitted it in 2017 with a new bar, a coffee lounge and a restaurant of around a hundred seats. Large windows look straight out over the bay, which is the stretch of sea where Barnes Wallis's bouncing bomb was tested in the Second World War. The kitchen leans towards seafood and local produce and serves breakfast, lunch and dinner, from classic fish and chips to burgers, salads and puddings. Cask beers include Shepherd Neame's own ales. Outside there is covered and open seating, and a kiosk sells ice creams and flatbread pizzas on fine days. Live music and a function room make it a hub for the Minnis Bay community, and it is a natural stop after a walk along the sea wall towards Reculver.
opening_hours: Per CAMRA (updated Sept 2025): Mon-Thu 09:00-22:00, Fri-Sat 09:00-23:00, Sun 09:00-22:00; food 09:00-11:00 and 12:00-21:00. Seafront kiosk 12:00-18:00 daily, weather permitting.
accessibility: Wheelchair access advertised by the venue
tips: Busy on sunny weekends; reviewers mention slow service at peak times, so book or come early. Pay-and-display car park right outside.

name: The Waves (bar, café and B&B)
summary: Relaxed bar-café with B&B rooms and plenty of outdoor tables looking over Minnis Bay.
description: The Waves sits on the corner of Hengist Road just back from the Minnis Bay promenade and works as a café by day and a casual bar into the evening. It is also a small bed and breakfast. Its main draw is the large outdoor terrace where you can sit with a coffee, a cold drink or a light meal and watch the windsurfers, kitesurfers and dinghies of the neighbouring sailing club out on the bay. The menu is casual seaside food, served from breakfast onwards, and the hours change with the seasons. It does not serve cask ale. Families and dogs are welcome, which makes it a handy alternative to the bigger Minnis Bay Bar & Brasserie a few doors away when that is full.
opening_hours: Per CAMRA (Aug 2025): bar Sun-Thu 10:00-20:00, Fri-Sat 10:00-22:00; food roughly 08:00-19:00 (to 20:00 Fri-Sat). Hours vary by season.
tips: Grab an outside table on a windy day to watch the kitesurfers.

name: The Windshack
summary: Small seasonal snack and coffee hut on the Minnis Bay promenade.
description: The Windshack is a little takeaway hut on the promenade at the western end of Minnis Bay, beside the beach huts and the start of the long sea-wall path towards Reculver. It is the kind of place you visit for a takeaway coffee, a cold drink, a snack or an ice cream while on the beach rather than for a sit-down meal. It held a top (5) food hygiene rating at its last inspection in June 2025. Opening is weather dependent and mostly in the warmer months, and published hours are hard to find, so treat it as a bonus if it is open. For a full meal or toilets, the Minnis Bay Bar & Brasserie and the public toilets are a short walk east along the front.
opening_hours: Not published; seasonal and weather dependent
tips: Do not rely on it out of season.

name: Old Bay Alehouse
summary: Award-winning micropub in a former shop near Minnis Bay, pouring real ale straight from the cask. In the Good Beer Guide 2026.
description: Old Bay Alehouse is one of Thanet's many micropubs: a single small room in what used to be a shop on Minnis Road, opened in March 2017. There is no lager font or jukebox; instead three or so changing real ales, at least one of them from a Kent brewery, are served by gravity from a temperature-controlled room behind the bar, alongside ciders and wine. Conversation is the entertainment. The pub has been listed in CAMRA's Good Beer Guide several times, including the 2026 edition, and was a runner-up in a micropub award in 2019. Food is limited to bar snacks, plus occasional pop-up nights such as a monthly curry evening that must be booked. Dogs and families are welcome, and the beach at Minnis Bay is about five minutes' walk away.
opening_hours: Per CAMRA (Mar 2025): Wed-Sat 16:00-21:00, Sun 12:00-16:00, closed Mon-Tue. Occasionally closed for private parties - check its social media.
tips: Small and short hours; arrive soon after opening on Friday or Saturday for a seat. Bus 32 stops close by.

name: Wagtails Cafe & Bar
summary: Small, friendly licensed café on Minnis Road with breakfasts, light lunches and cakes; dogs welcome.
description: Wagtails is a small neighbourhood café-bar on the Minnis Road parade a few minutes up from the beach at Minnis Bay, in the premises previously listed as Joe's Cafe. It is run by a small local team and serves hot drinks, cakes, snacks, breakfasts and light lunches, and it holds a licence so you can also have a glass of something. It takes part in the Chatty Cafe Scheme, which means there is a table set aside where anyone who fancies a chat is welcome to sit and talk, and local clubs and groups use it as a meeting place. Dogs are welcome and the café mentions free parking nearby. It received a top food hygiene rating in May 2026. Opening hours are not published online, so check before going out of your way.
opening_hours: Not published online
tips: Next door but one to the Old Bay Alehouse micropub.

name: The Parlour
summary: 1940s-themed café and ice cream parlour near the station, known for sundaes as well as breakfasts and lunches.
description: The Parlour is a café and ice cream parlour decorated in a 1940s style, at the bottom of Birchington's shopping street where Station Road turns into Minnis Road and heads down to Minnis Bay. It is a good halfway stop between the village centre and the beach. The menu covers breakfast, lunch and daily specials made with fresh, local ingredients, but the ice cream is the star: sundaes and other desserts are a speciality, and the café happily serves ice cream at any point in the meal. Groups are welcome. It is listed by Visit Thanet among the isle's ice cream parlours and held a top food hygiene rating in June 2026. Being just round the corner from Birchington-on-Sea station, it is easy to reach by train.
opening_hours: Tue-Sat 09:30-16:00 (Visit Thanet listing); closed Sun-Mon
tips: A three-minute walk from Birchington-on-Sea station.

name: Christies Wine Bar
summary: Wine bar with a pub feel opposite Birchington station; lunches, upstairs evening restaurant and weekend live music.
description: Despite the name, Christies feels more like a pub than a wine bar. It occupies a prominent building on Station Approach right by Birchington-on-Sea station, which makes it a convenient first or last stop for anyone arriving by train. Downstairs there are two handpumps, with Fuller's London Pride the usual cask beer, plus wines and spirits. Lunches are served daily, and upstairs there is a restaurant that opens in the evenings by booking only, along with a function room. Live music is a regular feature on weekend evenings. There is a garden and dogs are welcome. CAMRA lists it as open and it received a top food hygiene rating in July 2025.
opening_hours: Per CAMRA: Sun-Thu 11:00-21:00, Fri-Sat 11:00-23:00; food 12:00-15:00 daily; upstairs restaurant evenings by booking.
tips: Book ahead for the upstairs evening restaurant.

name: The Seaview
summary: Former Railway Hotel of 1865 near the station, with a big garden, sports screens, rooms and whale-bone garden feature.
description: The Seaview was built in 1865, two years after the railway reached Birchington, and was originally called the Railway Hotel. Over the years it has been a Charrington's house and then a Shepherd Neame pub, and it later absorbed the neighbouring Pond Cottage. Today it is a lively community local with four letting rooms, a function room and a large garden where sport is often shown on a big screen, as well as screens indoors. Look out in the garden for two old blocked-up wells and a decorative arch made from whale rib bones. Timothy Taylor Landlord is the regular cask beer. It stands on Station Road a short walk from the station and the shops, and it held a top food hygiene rating at its last inspection.
opening_hours: Per CAMRA (May 2025): Sun-Thu 12:00-23:00, Fri-Sat 12:00-00:00
tips: Ask to see the whale-bone feature in the garden.

name: The Wheel Alehouse
summary: Nautical-themed micropub on Station Road, one of Thanet's earliest (2013), known for craft beers and cheese boards.
description: The Wheel opened in March 2013 in a former shop on Birchington's Station Road, which makes it one of the earlier micropubs in Thanet, the area that helped spark the micropub movement. Inside it has a nautical theme. Rather than traditional cask ale it concentrates on keg-style craft beers and a range of specialist beers in cans and bottles. Food is mainly cheese boards drawn from a large selection of cheeses, with some evening meals. There is seating out front where smoking is allowed, sports on TV, occasional live music and Wi-Fi, and dogs are welcome. It held a top food hygiene rating in May 2026. It is roughly halfway between the Square and the station.
tips: Weekday opening is evenings only.

name: The Powell
summary: Birchington's oldest inn on the Square, Grade II listed, reopened July 2025 with a restaurant and boutique rooms.
description: The Powell (long known as the Powell Arms) faces All Saints' Church across the village Square and is Birchington's oldest hostelry. The present Grade II listed building dates from around 1840; it was once called the New Inn and was renamed after Squire Powell Powell of Quex Park, High Sheriff of Kent in 1823. Its upstairs room used to host parish meetings. After a spell closed it reopened in July 2025 with a mix of contemporary and traditional décor, a conservatory, a real fire, seating out front, a restaurant separate from the bar and six boutique bedrooms. Expect one regular cask ale, usually Doom Bar, and a changing local beer such as Wantsum's. Dogs and families are welcome. It makes a natural stop when visiting the church, where the Pre-Raphaelite painter Dante Gabriel Rossetti is buried.
opening_hours: Per CAMRA (updated Jan 2026): daily 12:00-23:00; check food times with the pub
tips: Combine with a look at All Saints' Church and Rossetti's grave opposite.

name: Fields Café
summary: Family-run café on the village Square serving homemade dishes from local produce, Wednesday to Sunday.
description: Fields Café is a family-run café in the heart of Birchington, on the Square opposite the church. The building spent many years as a pub before becoming a coffee shop; the current owners renamed it Fields and focus on homemade breakfasts, lunches and cakes, buying local produce wherever they can. It is a small, cosy place, popular with locals, and a good stop before or after exploring the church and the old village centre. Short-stay pay-and-display parking is available round the corner in the Albion Road car park. It received a top food hygiene rating at its last inspection in November 2024. Note that a sale listing for the business has appeared online, so it is worth checking it is still trading as Fields before you go.
opening_hours: Wed-Sat 09:00-15:00, Sun 10:00-15:00 (Visit Thanet listing); closed Mon-Tue
tips: Albion Road car park is the nearest parking.

name: Village Square Cafe
summary: Everyday café on Birchington's Square, handy for a cuppa and snack in the village centre.
description: The Village Square Cafe occupies a double shopfront on the Square in the middle of old Birchington, where the main road through the village meets Station Road and faces All Saints' Church and the Powell inn. It is a straightforward everyday café, the sort of place locals drop into for a cup of tea, a breakfast or a sandwich between errands. It received a top food hygiene rating at its July 2025 inspection. Opening hours are not published online, so assume daytime hours only. It is useful as a second option when Fields Café across the Square is closed, which is every Monday and Tuesday. The bus stops for Stagecoach routes 8 and 8A to Margate and Canterbury are a few steps away.
opening_hours: Not published online

name: The Cow Shed Bar & Grill
summary: Steak and burger restaurant on the Square: locally sourced steaks aged on the bone and burgers made in-house.
description: The Cow Shed opened on Birchington's Square in February 2018 after a six-month refit, and its owners also run a sister Cow Shed in Faversham. As the name suggests, it is all about beef: steaks come from local suppliers and are dry-aged on the bone for 28 days, and the burgers are minced and shaped in the kitchen from whole cuts several times a week. Vegetarian and vegan dishes are also offered. The bar carries cask ales, wines, spirits and a range of gins, and there is some outdoor seating. Listings put a typical spend in the £30-£49 a head range. A job advert in April 2026 for chefs at both sites suggests it is trading normally, and it was inspected for food hygiene in May 2026.
opening_hours: SquareMeal listing: daily 12:00-21:00 (not confirmed by the restaurant)
tips: Book at weekends.

name: The Smugglers
summary: Family-run Kentish restaurant in a 17th-century listed building just east of the Square; strong on Sunday roasts and steaks.
description: The Smugglers is a family-run restaurant in a Grade II listed building from the 1600s on Canterbury Road, a minute's walk east of Birchington Square. Its name nods to the smuggling that went on along this stretch of coast in the 18th century. Inside it has a traditional, beamed dining-room feel, and there are a few tables outside in good weather. The cooking is classic: reviewers single out the Sunday roasts, fillet steak, Chateaubriand for two and salmon dishes, and there is a children's menu. OpenTable puts a typical spend at around £26-£40 a head. It does not have private dining rooms, so it suits couples and small groups best. It held a top food hygiene rating at its August 2025 inspection, and it has a small customer car park.
opening_hours: Not confirmed; check the website or OpenTable
accessibility: Step-free access not stated; call ahead
tips: Book ahead, particularly for Sunday lunch.

name: Harbour Bakery & Driftwood Cafe
summary: Bakery with a small café on Birchington's Station Road for bread, pastries and a coffee.
description: Harbour Bakery and its Driftwood Cafe share a shopfront on the busy middle stretch of Station Road, Birchington's main shopping street between the Square and the railway station. It is a bakery first, so it is the place to pick up a loaf, a sausage roll or pastries for a picnic on the beach at Minnis Bay or Epple Bay, and there is a café side where you can sit with a coffee. It was most recently inspected for food hygiene in August 2026 and scored the top rating of 5, which also confirms it is currently trading. Opening hours are not published online; like most bakeries, expect it to open early and close by mid-afternoon. Several other independent food shops, including a deli, butcher and greengrocer, are within a few doors.
opening_hours: Not published online
tips: Stock up here for a beach picnic.

name: Mandy's Deli
summary: Independent delicatessen on Station Road, good for picnic supplies.
description: Mandy's Deli is an independent delicatessen on Birchington's Station Road, part of a cluster of small food shops on the stretch between the Square and the station. It is a useful stop for picnic supplies, sandwiches and treats before heading down to the beaches at Minnis Bay or Epple Bay. It received the top food hygiene rating of 5 at its April 2026 inspection, which shows it is currently trading. Detailed opening hours and a product list are not published online. Within a few doors you will also find a family butcher, a greengrocer and a bakery, so this stretch of Station Road is the best place in the village to put together a picnic from local independents rather than a supermarket.
opening_hours: Not published online

name: R C Wale & Son (butcher)
summary: Traditional family butcher on Birchington's Station Road.
description: R C Wale & Son is a traditional family butcher on Station Road in Birchington, one of a handful of independent food shops that keep the village's main street lively. It is the sort of shop locals use for their Sunday joint, sausages and barbecue meat, and visitors staying in self-catering cottages or caravans nearby will find it handy for the same. It was inspected for food hygiene in March 2026 and given the top rating of 5. Opening hours are not published online; as with most butchers, expect it to be open during the day from Monday to Saturday and closed on Sundays, but check locally. The neighbouring shops include a greengrocer, a deli and a bakery.
opening_hours: Not published online
tips: Useful for self-caterers and barbecues.

name: Monty's Greengrocers
summary: Independent greengrocer on Station Road for fruit, veg and picnic fruit.
description: Monty's is an independent greengrocer on Birchington's Station Road, near the station end of the shopping street. Thanet is a farming island as well as a seaside one, and greengrocers like this are the easiest way for a visitor to taste local fruit and vegetables in season, alongside the farm shop at Quex Barn a mile inland. It is a good stop for fruit to take down to the beach. It was inspected for food hygiene in July 2025 and given the top rating. Opening hours are not published online. Together with the butcher, deli and bakeries a few doors away, it makes Station Road a good place for self-caterers to shop locally.
opening_hours: Not published online

name: Minnis Bay Fish & Chips
summary: Fish and chip shop on Station Road near the station, on the way down to Minnis Bay.
description: Despite its name, Minnis Bay Fish & Chips is on Station Road near Birchington-on-Sea station rather than on the seafront, so it is a convenient place to pick up fish and chips on the way down Minnis Road to the beach, about fifteen minutes' walk away, or to eat on a bench in the village. It is a traditional chippy offering takeaway fish and chips. It was given the top food hygiene rating of 5 at its May 2025 inspection. Opening hours are not published online; most local chip shops open at lunchtime and again in the evening, with Sundays and Mondays the likeliest days off, but check before setting out. For a sit-down seafood meal by the sea, the Minnis Bay Bar & Brasserie is the alternative.
opening_hours: Not published online
tips: Takeaway to the beach is a 15-minute walk down Minnis Road.

name: Tandoori Nite
summary: Long-standing Indian restaurant and takeaway on Birchington's Station Road.
description: Tandoori Nite is an Indian restaurant and takeaway on Station Road in the middle of Birchington's shopping street. It serves the familiar British-Indian curry-house menu and is one of several evening options in the village, along with Chinese takeaways on the Square and on Station Road. It received the top food hygiene rating of 5 at its December 2024 inspection. Opening hours and a phone number are not published in the sources checked, so ring or check a delivery app before going. Being a few minutes from the station and close to the pubs on Station Road, it works well for an evening meal after a drink at the Wheel Alehouse or the Seaview.
opening_hours: Not confirmed

name: Quex Barn Farm Shop & Restaurant
summary: Award-winning farm shop, butcher, deli, fish stall, café and restaurant on the Quex Park estate.
description: Quex Barn is the farm shop of the Quex Park estate, the historic home of the Powell-Cotton family on the southern edge of Birchington. It sells produce from the estate's own farm and other local growers, and under one roof you will find a butchery, a delicatessen, a wet fish counter, a bakery, fruit and vegetables, flowers and a coffee shop. Alongside is a restaurant serving freshly cooked breakfasts and lunches from the same ingredients, plus a pizzeria. It was named Farm Shop of the Year in the Kent Life Food and Drink Awards 2019. The barn is a short walk from the Powell-Cotton Museum, Quex House and gardens, and the adventure play attractions in the park, so it is easy to make a day of it.
opening_hours: Farm shop & café: Mon and Sun 09:00-17:00, Tue-Sat 09:00-17:30. Restaurant: daily 09:00-15:00 (quexbarn.com, Oct 2026).
tips: Pair with the Powell-Cotton Museum; Felicity's Café opposite the museum closes at the end of October 2026, so Quex Barn is the main food stop on the estate.

name: Quince
summary: Michelin-listed neighbourhood bistro: Kentish produce with a southern Mediterranean accent and an English-leaning wine list.
description: Quince is the area's most acclaimed restaurant, a small bistro on Westgate's Station Road a minute from the station. The cooking is British bistro food built on ingredients from Kent farms, with a southern Mediterranean influence, and the short wine list gives English wines a prominent place next to bottles from elsewhere. It has been named among the Good Food Guide's 100 best local restaurants in Britain (2023 and 2024), featured in the Good Food Guide 2025, and is listed in the Michelin Guide 2025 and 2026. A set lunch is good value. It opens from Wednesday evening to Sunday lunch only, and booking is strongly advised. Westgate-on-Sea station is a short walk away.
opening_hours: Wed 18:00-21:00; Thu-Sat 12:00-15:00 and 18:00-21:00; Sun 12:00-15:00; closed Mon-Tue (Visit Thanet listing)
price: Set lunch £26 for 2 courses, £29.50 for 3 (Visit Thanet listing)
tips: Book well ahead for Friday and Saturday dinner.

name: The Bake & Alehouse
summary: Tiny, much-awarded micropub in Westgate with six to eight Kentish real ales served straight from the cask.
description: The Bake & Alehouse is a small micropub in former shop and office premises on St Mildred's Road, Westgate's main street, next to the Carlton Cinema. It seats only around eighteen people, and it serves six to eight real ales at a time, mostly from Kent breweries, poured straight from the cask, plus cider and a small range of premium spirits for those who do not drink beer. There is no music or TV; the point is good beer and conversation. The local CAMRA branch has given it many awards, including Thanet Pub of the Year in 2014 and Micropub of the Year in 2019 and 2020. Dogs are welcome and cards are accepted.
opening_hours: Per Thanet CAMRA: Mon, Wed, Thu, Sun 12:00-19:00; Fri-Sat 12:00-21:30; closed Tue
tips: Combine with a film at the Carlton Cinema next door.

name: Fredericks Tea Rooms
summary: Tea room in Westgate's Town Hall buildings known for homemade cakes, light lunches and afternoon tea.
description: Fredericks is a traditional tea room in the Town Hall buildings on St Mildred's Road, Westgate's main shopping street. The emphasis is on homemade cakes, with light lunches and afternoon tea also on offer, and vegetarian and gluten-free choices are available. It is a pleasant, unhurried stop after walking along the promenade at St Mildred's Bay or West Bay, both a few minutes away downhill. It received a top food hygiene rating in July 2026, so it is currently trading; its Visit Thanet listing notes that it reopened with revised hours, so check its website before visiting.
opening_hours: Visit Thanet listing: Mon-Sat 09:30-17:00 (revised hours - check before visiting)
tips: Good for afternoon tea after a seafront walk.

name: Staple Stores (bakery)
summary: Tiny artisan bakery-café hidden in an alley behind St Mildred's Road, famed for its pastries; Good Food Guide listed.
description: Staple Stores is a small artisan bakery group with branches around Thanet, and its Westgate outpost is famously hard to find: it is tucked away on St Mildred's Walk, a narrow lane behind the main St Mildred's Road shops. The bakers use traditional methods and seasonal ingredients to make bread and viennoiserie; reviewers rave about the pastries, the cheesecake and the cruffin, a croissant baked in a muffin tin and filled with crème pâtissière. There is a little café space for a coffee with your pastry. It is listed in the Good Food Guide 2025 and was rated 5 for food hygiene in July 2025. It opens early and closes early, and the best items can sell out, so aim for the morning.
address: 19 St Mildred's Walk (behind St Mildred's Road), Westgate-on-Sea
opening_hours: Published: Mon-Sat 08:00-14:30, Sun 08:00-13:00 (check before visiting)
tips: Look for the alley off St Mildred's Road; go early before items sell out. The map point marks the lane, not the door.

name: Dadd's Family Butchers
summary: Family butcher on Westgate's St Mildred's Road.
description: Dadd's is a family butcher on St Mildred's Road, Westgate's main shopping street, and one of the independent food shops that give the small town centre its character. It is the place in Westgate to buy meat for a barbecue or a self-catering roast. It was inspected for food hygiene in May 2026 and awarded the top rating of 5. Opening hours are not published online; expect normal daytime shop hours from Monday to Saturday. Close by are Staple Stores bakery in the lane behind the shops, a greengrocer on Station Road, the Bake & Alehouse micropub and Fredericks Tea Rooms, so it is easy to combine a bit of shopping with a coffee or a drink.
opening_hours: Not published online

name: J. Prentis Greengrocers
summary: Westgate greengrocer on Station Road, open seven days.
description: J. Prentis is a traditional greengrocer on the eastern part of Station Road in Westgate-on-Sea, close to the station bridge. It sells fruit and vegetables and is a handy place to pick up fruit for the beach at St Mildred's Bay or West Bay, both a few minutes' walk away. Its opening hours as recorded on OpenStreetMap are early-morning starts from Monday to Saturday and a short Sunday morning session, which is more generous than many small shops. It was inspected for food hygiene in July 2026 and rated 5. Nearby on the same parade are bakeries, cafés, a pizza restaurant and a curry house, plus the Co-op for anything else.
opening_hours: Mon-Sat 07:00-17:00, Sun 10:00-14:00 (OpenStreetMap record; not confirmed by shop)

name: Hot Wood Pizza
summary: Pizza restaurant on Westgate's Station Road parade.
description: Hot Wood Pizza is a pizza restaurant on the Station Road parade in Westgate-on-Sea, among the cluster of cafés, takeaways and shops just east of the station. It is a casual option for families wanting an easy evening meal after a day on the beach at St Mildred's Bay, which is a short walk north. It was inspected for food hygiene in February 2026 and awarded the top rating of 5. A menu, phone number and opening hours were not available in the sources checked, so look it up on a delivery app or call in. For something more formal, Quince bistro is on the same road a little to the west, and the Swan by the Sea overlooks West Bay.
opening_hours: Not confirmed

name: Regency Tandoori
summary: Indian restaurant and takeaway on Westgate's Station Road, open lunch and evening.
description: Regency Tandoori is an Indian restaurant and takeaway on the Station Road parade in Westgate-on-Sea, a couple of minutes from the station. It offers the familiar British-Indian menu of tandoori dishes, curries and breads, for eating in or taking away. According to the opening hours recorded on OpenStreetMap it serves a lunchtime session and then evenings until late, with slightly later closing on Fridays and Saturdays, which makes it one of the later options in Westgate. It was inspected for food hygiene in August 2026 and rated 5. It is a good fallback if Quince is fully booked or closed on a Monday or Tuesday.
opening_hours: Daily 12:00-14:00; evenings Sun-Thu 17:30-23:00, Fri-Sat 17:30-23:30 (OpenStreetMap record; check before visiting)

name: The Best Beano Cafe
summary: All-day breakfast café on Westgate's Station Road, open seven days from early morning.
description: The Best Beano is a traditional British café on Westgate's Station Road parade, the kind of place for a full English breakfast, a mug of tea and simple lunches. Opening hours recorded on OpenStreetMap start at 7am on weekdays and Saturdays and 8am on Sundays, which makes it one of the earliest places to get breakfast in Westgate, useful before an early train or a morning on the beach at St Mildred's Bay. It was given the top food hygiene rating of 5 in February 2025. There is a separate Beano Cafe a few doors along at number 5D, which was also inspected and rated 5 in September 2026; do not confuse the two.
opening_hours: Mon-Sat 07:00-18:00, Sun 08:00-18:00, bank holidays 08:00-17:00 (OpenStreetMap record)
tips: Early breakfast before the train.

name: Westgate Fish Bar
summary: Fish and chip shop on Westgate's Station Road near the station.
description: Westgate Fish Bar is the fish and chip shop on Station Road in Westgate-on-Sea, a few doors from the railway station. Its menu is traditional chip-shop fare: battered fish and chips plus pies such as beef and onion and chicken and mushroom. It is a five-minute walk downhill to the promenade at St Mildred's Bay or West Bay if you want to eat by the sea. It was inspected in July 2026 and given the top food hygiene rating of 5. Opening hours and a phone number were not available from the sources checked. Another chip shop, The Fish Inn, is on Cambourne Avenue on the south side of the railway.
opening_hours: Not confirmed
tips: Take it down to the West Bay promenade for sunset.

name: The Fish Inn
summary: Neighbourhood fish and chip takeaway on Cambourne Avenue, south Westgate.
description: The Fish Inn is a fish and chip takeaway on the small Cambourne Avenue shopping parade in the residential southern part of Westgate-on-Sea, on the other side of the railway and the A28 from the seafront. It is mainly a local's chippy, but it is handy if you are staying in the holiday lets or caravan parks around the southern side of Westgate and Birchington, or are driving along the Canterbury Road. It received the top food hygiene rating of 5 at its May 2025 inspection. Opening hours were not available from the sources checked. A Chinese takeaway, New Friendly House, is next door at number 28.
opening_hours: Not confirmed

name: Paul's Bar & Bistro
summary: Bar and bistro on Westgate's Station Road, opposite the station area.
description: Paul's Bar & Bistro is a bar-restaurant on Station Road in Westgate-on-Sea, close to the station and on the same stretch as Quince and Ginger's. It offers a relaxed place for a drink and a meal in the town centre rather than on the seafront. It was inspected for food hygiene in July 2026 and awarded the top rating of 5, which confirms it is currently operating. A menu, phone number and opening hours were not available from the sources checked, so check locally. If you want a meal with a sea view instead, the Swan by the Sea at West Bay and the St Mildred's Bay restaurant on the promenade are each about five to ten minutes' walk away.
opening_hours: Not confirmed

name: Ginger's
summary: Small evening bar on Westgate's Station Road, open Thursday to Sunday.
description: Ginger's is a small bar on Station Road in Westgate-on-Sea that opens in the evenings towards the end of the week. It is registered as a pub/bar and was inspected for food hygiene in January 2026, receiving the top rating of 5. Opening hours recorded on OpenStreetMap are Thursday to Sunday from 5.30pm until late evening. It is a modern alternative to the town's traditional real-ale micropub, the Bake & Alehouse, which is a few minutes' walk away on St Mildred's Road. Further details such as the drinks range were not available from the sources checked, so treat it as a place to discover locally.
opening_hours: Thu-Sun 17:30-23:30 (OpenStreetMap record; not confirmed by venue)

name: The Swan by the Sea
summary: Large food-led pub overlooking Westgate's West Bay, with Sunday roasts and Kentish ales.
description: The Swan is a large pub just above West Bay in Westgate-on-Sea, now trading as the Swan by the Sea. It is food-led, with lunch and dinner served in the bar and restaurant and Sunday roasts from midday to 4pm. The regular cask beers are Fuller's London Pride and Gadds' No. 5 from Ramsgate's own brewery, with a third ale added in summer and busy periods. Facilities include a garden, real fire, function room, games, sport on TV, occasional live music and its own car park. Families and dogs are welcome. Its position at the top of West Bay makes it the obvious place for a meal or a pint after watching the sunset from the west-facing promenade.
opening_hours: Per Thanet CAMRA: Mon-Thu 12:00-21:00, Fri-Sat 12:00-23:00, Sun 12:00-21:00; Sunday roasts 12:00-16:00
tips: Public toilets are on the West Bay promenade just below.

name: West Bay Cafe
summary: Dog-friendly promenade café on West Bay with breakfasts, ice cream and sunset views.
description: The West Bay Cafe sits on the promenade at West Bay, the sandy beach on the western side of Westgate-on-Sea. Because the bay faces west, it is one of the best spots on this coast to watch the sun go down over the sea. The menu is honest seaside café food: all-day breakfasts, homemade meals, vegetarian and vegan options, ice creams, milkshakes and fresh coffee. Dogs are welcome, with water and treats provided, though they must be on a lead inside; note that dogs are banned from West Bay beach itself from 10am to 6pm between May and September. Upstairs is Finbars, a small restaurant. It held a top food hygiene rating at its October 2024 inspection.
opening_hours: Listed as open daily from 09:00 (closing times vary by season)
dogs: Dog friendly inside on a lead; seasonal beach dog ban applies
tips: Stay for sunset; parking is on-street along Sea Road.

name: Finbars Restaurant
summary: Small restaurant upstairs at the West Bay Cafe, overlooking the bay.
description: Finbars is a small restaurant on the floor above the West Bay Cafe on the Westgate promenade, so it shares the café's view out over West Bay and the sunsets that make this beach special. Reviewers describe it as small but very good, and it offers a more grown-up evening alternative to the café downstairs. It was inspected for food hygiene in September 2025 and rated 5, so it is trading. A menu, phone line and opening hours of its own were not available from the sources checked; use the café's number to ask. Booking is sensible given the limited number of tables.
address: Above West Bay Cafe, Sea Road, Westgate-on-Sea
opening_hours: Not confirmed
tips: Ask for a window table at sunset.

name: The St Mildred's Bay
summary: Highly rated seafront bistro on the St Mildred's Bay promenade: breakfasts, seafood sharers, roasts and a terrace.
description: The St Mildred's Bay is a seafront restaurant on the promenade at St Mildred's Bay, the main beach of Westgate-on-Sea. It serves from breakfast through to dinner, with a menu ranging from snacks and light bites to seafood sharing platters, fish and chips and hearty Sunday roasts, and there is an outdoor terrace overlooking the sand. It is one of the best reviewed places in the area on OpenTable, with several hundred reviews averaging close to five stars, and it is dog friendly. A pay-and-display car park and public toilets are right beside it. Its listing shows it under the same address as Millie's Beach Bar.
address: St Mildred's Gardens, St Mildred's Bay, Westgate-on-Sea
opening_hours: Listed (AAA): Mon-Sat 08:30-20:15, Sun 08:30-17:45; hours vary between listings, check before visiting
tips: Book on OpenTable for weekends; St Mildred's Bay car park is free for cars Nov-Mar.

name: The Sun Inn
summary: Friendly village pub on The Street in St Nicholas-at-Wade with food, garden and changing real ales.
description: St Nicholas-at-Wade is a quiet farming village on the old shoreline of the Wantsum Channel, which once made Thanet a true island, and it has kept two pubs on its main street. The Sun is the later of them, a red-brick building from around 1900, and it reopened under new management in late August 2021. It serves lunches every day and evening meals from Tuesday to Saturday, has a restaurant area, a garden, a real fire and parking, and welcomes dogs. Two changing real ales are typically on, such as London Pride or Harvey's Sussex Best. It received a top food hygiene rating in June 2026. Combine a visit with the village's medieval flint church of St Nicholas, a short walk away.
opening_hours: Per CAMRA (Mar 2026): daily 12:00-15:00 and 17:00-23:00. Food: lunch 12:00-14:30 daily; evenings Tue-Sat 18:00-20:00.
tips: Stagecoach 8/8A between Margate and Canterbury stop near the village.

name: The Bell Inn
summary: Grade II listed village local with Tudor roots and a nationally important historic interior; Sunday lunches.
description: The Bell is the older of St Nicholas-at-Wade's two pubs and a real treat for anyone interested in historic pubs. Behind its 19th-century frontage is a timber-framed core of the 1600s, and CAMRA lists its interior as being of special national historic interest: there are four rooms, fittings from the 1930s and hand-pumps dated 1937, plus a post-war extension modernised in 2020. The building is Grade II listed. It is a traditional village local with a garden, real fires, parking and regular live music, and the Bell hosts the village wassail in January, an old custom of blessing the apple trees. Food is served on Sundays. It was rated 5 for food hygiene in March 2026.
tips: Explore the different rooms to see the old fittings.

name: Wantsum Brewery Tap & The Kent Barn
summary: Taproom of Thanet's Wantsum Brewery on a farm outside St Nicholas-at-Wade; weekend opening, beer shop, garden.
description: Wantsum Brewery takes its name from the Wantsum Channel, the stretch of water that once separated Thanet from mainland Kent, and its brewery and tap occupy farm buildings at St Nicholas Court Farm just outside the village of St Nicholas-at-Wade. In the taproom you can drink three or so of the brewery's changing cask beers and real cider, indoors or in the garden, and there is a shop selling bottles to take away. It is family and dog friendly, has parking, a pool table and a crokinole board, and runs occasional food and a summer beer festival. Opening is at weekends only. It is about 1.4 km from the nearest bus stop, so most visitors drive or cycle.
address: The Kent Barn, St Nicholas Court Farm, Court Road, St Nicholas-at-Wade
opening_hours: Per CAMRA (Mar 2026): taproom Fri-Sat 14:00-20:00, Sun 12:00-18:00, closed Mon-Thu. Shop: Mon-Thu 12:00-16:00, Fri-Sat 14:00-20:00, Sun 11:00-17:00.
tips: Designate a driver or cycle; the nearest bus (8/8A) is a 15-20 minute walk.

name: The King Ethelbert Inn
summary: Family-run freehouse beside Reculver Towers and the Roman fort, with log burners, terrace and Sunday roasts.
description: The King Ethelbert stands a stone's throw from the twin towers of Reculver's ruined church and the remains of the Roman fort, at the western end of the coastal path from Minnis Bay. It is named after the Anglo-Saxon king of Kent who is linked with the arrival of Christianity in England. The pub is a family-run freehouse serving traditional food made with local ingredients where possible, and changing local ales. Sunday roasts are served through the afternoon, and you can pre-order when booking. There are two log burners for winter, a decked terrace with covered seating and an enclosed children's play area, and dogs are very welcome. The pub also has a holiday let. The bouncing bomb was tested just offshore.
opening_hours: Shown only as an image on the pub's website; call to check. Sunday roasts 12:00-19:30.
tips: A natural end point for the coastal walk or cycle west from Minnis Bay.

name: HatHats Coffee, Reculver
summary: Kent coffee company's café at Reculver Country Park visitor centre: coffee, cakes, dog-friendly seating, open 364 days.
description: HatHats is a Kent coffee company founded in 2015, and its Reculver branch is in the Reculver Country Park visitor centre, right next to the Reculver Towers and Roman fort. It is popular with walkers and cyclists exploring the coast. Expect good coffee, homemade cakes, snacks and vegan options, with a dog-friendly seating area. The site has a pay-and-display car park, baby-changing toilets and a Changing Places toilet nearby, and wheelchair access. It opens every day of the year except Christmas Day, with longer hours in summer. Service can be slow at busy times, according to some reviewers.
address: Reculver Country Park Visitor Centre, Reculver Lane, Herne Bay
opening_hours: Summer (clocks forward): daily 08:00-19:00. Winter: Mon-Fri 08:00-16:00, Sat-Sun 08:00-17:00. Open 364 days.
accessibility: Wheelchair access; Changing Places toilet nearby
tips: Good refuelling stop at the end of the cycle or walk from Minnis Bay.

name: Angela's of Margate
summary: Sustainable seafood restaurant by Margate seafront with a daily-changing menu; Michelin Green Star holder.
description: Angela's is a small seafood restaurant in Margate's Old Town, just back from the harbour and Turner Contemporary. Its menu changes every day according to what the boats have landed that morning, served simply with seasonal vegetables. The restaurant is known for its commitment to sustainability: it sources seafood ethically, has worked to cut plastic out of its supply chain and sends its food waste to a community garden for compost. That has earned it a Michelin Green Star (2021, 2022 and 2024), and it is listed in the Michelin Guide 2026 and Harden's 2026. It serves lunch and dinner daily, and booking is recommended. Trains from Birchington to Margate take under ten minutes.
opening_hours: Daily: lunch from 12:00, dinner from 18:00 (Visit Thanet listing)
tips: Reserve ahead; combine with Turner Contemporary nearby.

name: Sargasso
summary: Seafood and vegetable small plates on Margate Harbour Arm, from the team behind Brawn; Michelin Bib Gourmand.
description: Sargasso occupies one of the old units on Margate's Harbour Arm, the stone pier that curls out from the Old Town, so diners look straight out over the sea and the sunsets. It was opened by the people behind Brawn in east London and serves seasonal coastal cooking as small plates for sharing, built on seafood and vegetables, with a list of natural and low-intervention wines and good music. It holds a Michelin Bib Gourmand (listed for 2022 and 2026). Bench tables can be booked for up to four, couples can sit at the bar, and there is part-covered seating outside; walk-ins are welcome when there is room. From autumn the lunch service is cut back to Friday to Monday.
address: Unit 13, Margate Harbour Arm, Stone Pier, Margate
opening_hours: Winter pattern per Visit Thanet: lunch Fri-Mon 12:00-15:30; dinner Fri-Sat 17:30-21:30, Sun-Mon 17:30-20:30. Summer: lunch and dinner daily.
tips: Book via the website; arrive for sunset over the harbour.

name: Bottega Caruso & Cantina Caruso
summary: Campanian home cooking with Kent produce in Margate Old Town; the Cantina deli-wine bar is a Good Food Guide regional winner.
description: Bottega Caruso was founded by Harry and Simona to share the food and recipes of Simona's home village, Foglianise in Campania, southern Italy, combining Italian ingredients with produce from Kent. The restaurant in Broad Street serves homemade pasta and regional dishes and has been in the Michelin Guide and the Good Food Guide. A few doors along, its sister Cantina Caruso is a deli and wine bar selling fresh pasta, ragù, sauces, cheeses, olive oil and natural wines by the glass or bottle; it was ranked second in the Good Food Guide's 100 Best Local Restaurants 2026 and named South East regional winner. Both are in the lanes of Margate's Old Town, a few minutes from the seafront.
address: 2-4 Broad Street (Cantina at 8 Broad Street), Margate
opening_hours: Restaurant Wed-Sat 12:00-15:00 and 18:00-21:00. Cantina shop Wed-Thu 11:00-17:00, Fri-Sat 11:00-22:00, Sun 12:00-16:00; bar Fri evening and Sat-Sun (Visit Thanet listing).
tips: Book the restaurant; the Cantina is good for a walk-in glass and Italian picnic shopping.

name: GB Pizza Co
summary: Award-winning wood-fired pizza on Margate seafront using British cheeses, meats and seasonal produce since 2012.
description: GB Pizza Co opened on Margate's seafront, Marine Drive, in October 2012 and has collected awards and guidebook listings ever since, including the Good Food Guide 2025 and Harden's 2026. The idea is wood-fired pizza with a British accent: thin, crisp bases topped with British cheeses, cured meats and seasonal produce, with British beers, apple juice and house wine to drink. It has seating inside and out, looking across to Margate Sands, and it welcomes groups and pets. Prices are moderate, which makes it one of the best family-friendly options in Margate. Opening is reduced in the autumn and winter months.
opening_hours: From 21 Sept 2026: Mon-Thu 16:00-21:00, Fri-Sat 12:00-21:00, Sun 12:00-18:00 (Visit Thanet listing)
tips: Weekday lunchtimes closed in the winter season.

name: Buoy and Oyster
summary: Seafood restaurant and oyster bar on the corner of Margate seafront, with a beachfront chip kiosk, Beach Buoys.
description: Buoy and Oyster is a seafood restaurant and oyster bar at the bottom of Margate's High Street where it meets the seafront, facing the Main Sands. Its menu is built around fish and shellfish, with oysters a speciality, and it also does Sunday roasts and afternoon teas. It is listed in Harden's 2026 restaurant guide. Above the restaurant are four apartments let as Margate Suites, two of them with sea views. Its sister operation, Beach Buoys, is a fish and chip takeaway kiosk on the beachfront nearby, open from Thursday to Sunday at the time of checking. The restaurant's website does not list hours, so book online or check before visiting.
opening_hours: Not published on website; book online. Beach Buoys kiosk Thu-Sun (website, Oct 2026).
tips: Beach Buoys is the quick takeaway option for fish and chips on the sand.

name: The Two Halves
summary: Seafront micropub on Marine Drive with sea views, cask ales and no TV or music; CAMRA Thanet Pub of the Year 2018 and 2022.
description: The Two Halves opened in 2015 in a small seafront unit on Margate's Marine Drive, about five minutes' walk from the station, and quickly became one of the town's best-loved pubs. True to the micropub idea, there is no television or music; people come for cask real ale, craft beer, cider and wine, conversation and the view over Margate Sands. It has featured in CAMRA's Good Beer Guide (2020, 2021 and 2025) and was named Thanet CAMRA Pub of the Year in 2018 and 2022, as well as Micropub of the Year 2022. It opens in the afternoon on weekdays and from lunchtime at weekends. It is a good place to finish a day in Margate before the short train ride back to Birchington.
opening_hours: Weekdays from 15:00, weekends from 13:00, closing 22:30 (Visit Thanet listing)
tips: Five minutes from Margate station.

name: The Mechanical Elephant (Wetherspoon)
summary: Wetherspoon pub on Margate seafront named after a petrol-driven elephant that once gave rides on the promenade; Good Beer Guide 2026.
description: This Wetherspoon pub on Marine Terrace faces Margate Sands and Dreamland's end of the seafront. Its curious name recalls a life-size mechanical elephant, powered by a petrol engine, that once carried children along the promenade. The building itself was made up of early Victorian seaside lodging houses; most of it was for many years the shop of William Robinson, confectioner, and the end unit was a restaurant. Expect the usual Wetherspoon formula of low prices, food from breakfast onwards and a good range of real ales, which has earned it a place in CAMRA's Good Beer Guide 2026. There is a licensed outside area, Wi-Fi and step-free access. Under-18s are allowed until 9pm.
tips: Cheap breakfast with a sea view before a day at Dreamland.

name: Mori Mori
summary: Cliftonville restaurant on Northdown Road ranked 48th in the Good Food Guide's 100 Best Local Restaurants 2026.
description: Mori Mori is on Northdown Road in Cliftonville, Margate's eastern district, where a run of independent food and drink places has opened in recent years. It was ranked 48th in the Good Food Guide's list of Britain's 100 Best Local Restaurants for 2026 and also appears in the Good Food Guide 2025, which puts it among the most highly regarded places to eat on the isle. Details of its menu, opening times and booking were not checked for this entry, so visit its website before going. Cliftonville lies just east of Margate's Old Town.
opening_hours: Not confirmed; see website
tips: Book ahead given its guide ranking.

name: Morelli's Gelato, Broadstairs
summary: Famous retro Italian ice cream parlour of 1932 overlooking Viking Bay, with booths, soda fountain and jukebox.
description: Morelli's is one of the most famous ice cream parlours in England. The Morelli family started their ice cream business in 1907 and still run it, and the Broadstairs coffee bar on Victoria Parade opened in 1932. Inside it is gloriously retro, with pink leatherette booths, Formica tables, a soda fountain and a jukebox. Ice cream is made on site, and mint choc chip and pistachio are the most popular flavours, with vegan choices too. It also serves coffee, cakes, pastries, Italian savouries and prosecco, and it looks out over Viking Bay. There is a second Morelli's on Margate seafront.
opening_hours: Mon-Fri 08:00-17:00, Sat-Sun 08:00-18:00 (Visit Thanet listing)
tips: Grab a booth by the window for the Viking Bay view.

name: Chiappini's
summary: 1950s-style ice cream parlour and coffee bar on Broadstairs promenade above the harbour and Viking Bay.
description: Chiappini's is an ice cream parlour and coffee bar on The Parade, the promenade above Broadstairs harbour and Viking Bay. It has a 1950s look and is the other half of Broadstairs' famous pair of Italian-style ice cream parlours, the first being Morelli's a short walk south. Ice cream is the main event, but it also serves coffee, meals and snacks, so it works for lunch as well as a sundae. The view down over the harbour, the pier and the beach huts of Viking Bay is one of the best in town. It is open every day, staying open later at weekends.
opening_hours: Mon-Fri 09:00-16:00, Sat-Sun 09:00-18:00 (Visit Thanet listing)
tips: Compare it with Morelli's - locals have their favourite.

name: Kebbells Seafood Bar
summary: Michelin-listed seafood bar on Broadstairs seafront, Kent Life Best Seafood winner 2025; oysters, small plates, lobster.
description: Kebbells is a seafood bar on Victoria Parade, Broadstairs' seafront, a couple of minutes from Viking Bay and next to Morelli's. The menu runs from oysters at the raw bar through small plates such as cured mackerel and stuffed squid to sharing dishes like mussels or lobster with chips, with a specials board and gelato for dessert. It is listed in the Michelin Guide 2026 and Harden's 2026, and in the Kent Life Food and Drink Awards 2025 it won Best Seafood, Best Use of Local Produce and Best Bar, and was highly commended for its chef, service, dog-friendliness and as Restaurant of the Year. It opens for lunch and dinner from Tuesday, and all day at weekends.
opening_hours: Tue-Thu 12:00-15:00 and 18:00-21:00; Fri-Sun 10:00-21:00; Mon not listed (Visit Thanet listing)
dogs: Highly commended as Best for Dogs (Kent Life 2025)
tips: Book for weekend evenings.

name: The Tartar Frigate
summary: 18th-century flint pub on Broadstairs harbour with an upstairs seafood restaurant looking over Viking Bay.
description: The Tartar Frigate is a flint-walled pub right on Broadstairs harbour. The current building dates from the 18th century, though there has been an inn on the site since Elizabethan times, and it is named after HMS Tartar, a frigate built in the town's shipyard. Downstairs is a cosy harbourside bar with live music on several evenings a week; upstairs is a seafood restaurant whose windows look over the harbour and Viking Bay, well regarded locally and best booked ahead. On summer evenings people take drinks out onto the harbour wall. The upstairs restaurant has no disabled access because of the age of the building.
opening_hours: Restaurant Mon-Sat 12:00-13:45 and 19:00-21:15; Sun two sittings 12:30 and 15:30 (Visit Thanet listing). Pub listed by CAMRA as 11:00-23:00 daily.
accessibility: No disabled access to the upstairs restaurant
tips: Phone numbers differ between listings (01843 862013 / 01843 601636).

name: The Magnet Micropub
summary: Broadstairs micropub named Kent Life Pub of the Year 2025; ales, ciders, gins, live music, dogs and kids welcome.
description: The Magnet is a micropub on Albion Street in the centre of Broadstairs, a couple of minutes from the harbour. It serves a changing range of ales and ciders plus gins and traditional pub snacks, and it has a friendly, community feel, with board games, regular live music and even a weekly knitting and crochet group. Dogs and children are welcome. It has been in CAMRA's Good Beer Guide every year from 2024 to 2026 and has won CAMRA's Traditional Pub of the Year, and in the Kent Life Food and Drink Awards 2025 it was named Pub of the Year and Best for Dogs. It is open every day from midday.
opening_hours: Mon-Thu 12:00-22:30, Fri-Sat 12:00-23:00, Sun 12:00-22:00 (Visit Thanet listing)

name: Royal Victoria Pavilion (Wetherspoon)
summary: Restored 1903 Grade II seaside pavilion on Ramsgate Main Sands, now said to be the UK's largest Wetherspoon.
description: The Royal Victoria Pavilion was built in 1903 to designs by Stanley Davenport Adshead and spent its working life as a seaside entertainment hall, later a cinema, nightclub and casino, before closing in 2008 and falling derelict. Wetherspoon restored the Grade II listed building at a reported cost of about £4.5 million and opened it as a pub in August 2017; it is widely described as the company's biggest pub in the UK, with two floors, two large bars and around 350 tables. A further refurbishment in 2023 added a glazed extension to the beachfront terrace. Seating on the terrace and on the first-floor roof deck looks over Ramsgate Main Sands and the Royal Harbour. Orders are taken through the Wetherspoon app. Dogs are not allowed, except assistance dogs.
opening_hours: Sun-Thu 08:00-00:00, Fri-Sat 08:00-01:00 (Visit Ramsgate listing)
tips: Head upstairs to the roof deck for the harbour view.

name: Marc-Pierre's Kitchen
summary: Modern European restaurant overlooking Ramsgate Royal Harbour, cooking local seasonal produce and local fish.
description: Marc-Pierre's Kitchen sits in Westcliff Arcade, the Victorian arcade set into the cliff above Ramsgate's Royal Harbour, so its windows look down over the yachts and fishing boats. The cooking is a contemporary take on classic European dishes with some fusion touches, based on local, seasonal and sustainable ingredients, including fish from a local fisherman, and everything is made on the premises. The menu is deliberately short, with half a dozen starters, about ten mains and four desserts plus a specials board. It is listed in Harden's 2026 restaurant guide. It opens Tuesday evening to Sunday lunchtime, with lunch on several days, and is closed on Mondays.
opening_hours: Tue from 17:30; Wed-Thu 11:30-14:00 and from 17:30; Fri-Sat from 11:30; last orders 21:30; Sun from 12:00 (last orders 16:00); Mon not listed (Visit Thanet listing)
tips: Ask for a harbour-view table.

name: The Montefiore Arms
summary: Back-street Ramsgate local in the CAMRA Good Beer Guide 2026.
description: The Montefiore Arms is a traditional back-street pub on Trinity Place in Ramsgate, a little inland from the harbour. A historic synagogue associated with Moses Montefiore stands a short walk away. The pub is listed in CAMRA's Good Beer Guide 2026, one of several Ramsgate entries in that guide, which makes it a good choice for real-ale fans exploring the town. Opening hours and facilities were not checked for this entry, so look at its website before going. Ramsgate station and the harbour are both within walking distance.
opening_hours: Not confirmed; see website
